origin.description: A zooreg is regular. strict still inspects the steps. A plain series is regular when the steps are integer multiples of the smallest step, or when the steps themselves are integers. One observation is not regular unless it is a zooreg. The default method checks 1 through NROW.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A zoo series stores observations separately from its index.

arguments.name: strict
arguments.text: If true, every step must match the first step. If false, every step may be an integer multiple of the smallest step.

origin.details: A zooreg is regular. strict still inspects the steps. A plain series is regular when the steps are integer multiples of the smallest step, or when the steps themselves are integers. One observation is not regular unless it is a zooreg. The default method checks 1 through NROW.
origin.value: TRUE when the series is regular, or strictly regular.
origin.example:
z <- zoo(1:10, seq(2000, 2002.25, by = 0.25))
cat(paste(as.numeric(c(is.regular(z), is.regular(z, strict = TRUE), is.regular(z[-3]), is.regular(z[-3], strict = TRUE))), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.details: A zooreg is regular. strict still inspects the steps. A plain series is regular when the steps are integer multiples of the smallest step, or when the steps themselves are integers. One observation is not regular unless it is a zooreg. The default method checks 1 through NROW.
translation.value: TRUE when the series is regular, or strictly regular.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.is_regular import is_regular
idx = [2000 + 0.25 * i for i in range(10)]
z = Zoo(np.arange(1, 11), idx)
omit = Zoo(np.arange(1, 10), idx[:2] + idx[3:])
flags = [is_regular(z), is_regular(z, True), is_regular(omit), is_regular(omit, True)]
print(" ".join("1" if flag else "0" for flag in flags))
